name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation
description: Black immediately contests d4 with e5, cramping White's center while developing the knight to c6.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Bielefelder Gambit
description: White captures e5 and Black develops the bishop to c5, seizing the initiative on light squares.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, de Smet Gambit
description: Black accepts the pawn trade and plays d6 to attack e5, preparing to recapture and reopen lines.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Hammer Gambit
description: Black aggressively attacks e5 with f6, opening kingside lines at the cost of pawn structure.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Herford Gambit
description: Black immediately develops the queen to h4 with tempo, threatening White's exposed kingside.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Keres Attack
description: Black recaptures with the knight and White develops with tempo via Nc3, supporting the centre.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Linksspringer Variation
description: White bypasses e5 and advances d5 instead, gaining space and displacing Black's centralized knight.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Main Line
description: White plays f4 to dislodge the centralized knight; Black retreats to g6 and regroups.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Paulsen Attack
description: White develops naturally with Nf3, attacking the e5 knight and consolidating the centre.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Kennedy Variation, Riemann Defense
description: White plays f4 to support the centre; Black's knight retreats to c6, maintaining flexibility.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Mikenas Variation
description: Black plays d6 for a flexible setup, preparing a kingside fianchetto or d5 breaks.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Neo-Mongoloid Defense
description: Black plays f6 to prepare e5 or d5 breaks while maintaining solid kingside structure.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Pirc Connection
description: Black fianchettoes the kingside with g6, preparing to control the long diagonal with the bishop.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Pseudo-Spanish Variation
description: White pins the knight with Bb5 in Ruy Lopez style, using Nc6 as leverage instead of Nf6.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation
description: Black immediately strikes at e4 with d5, leading to early central exchanges and simplification.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Aachen Gambit
description: Black plays Nb4 to attack d4 after White captures on d5, maintaining active piece counterplay.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Advance Variation
description: White advances e5 instead of capturing, closing the position and restricting Black's piece activity.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation
description: Black captures on e4 with Nc3 supporting White's centre; White maintains development tempo.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Brandics Gambit
description: Black plays a6 instead of recapturing, preparing b5 and queenside expansion against White's initiative.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Erben Gambit
description: Black fianchettoes with g6, aiming for long-diagonal control despite White's space advantage.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Heinola-Deppe Gambit
description: Black counterattacks with e5 instead of recapturing, creating central tension and complications.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Nimzowitsch Gambit
description: White advances d5 and Black plays Ne5, leading to dynamic tactical interplay in the centre.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Richter Gambit
description: White pushes d5 forcing Nb8, then plays f3 to secure the centre and prepare kingside assault.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Bogoljubow Variation, Vehre Variation
description: Black develops Nf6 instead of recapturing, maintaining piece activity and central flexibility.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Exchange Variation
description: White exchanges pawns and Black recaptures with the queen, centralizing it immediately for play.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Scandinavian Variation, Exchange Variation, Marshall Gambit
description: White develops Nc3 to attack the centralised queen and contest d5 after early exchanges.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Wheeler Gambit
description: White plays b4 immediately, offering the queenside pawn to disrupt Black's piece coordination.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Williams Variation
description: White develops Nf3 and Black plays d6, establishing flexibility with fianchetto and central options.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense: Woodchuck Variation
description: Black plays a6 early, preparing queenside expansion with b5 while centralizing the knight.

name: Owen Defense: Guatemala Defense
description: Black fianchettoes the queenside with b6, placing the bishop on a6 to control the long diagonal.

name: Owen Defense: Hekili-Loa Gambit
description: Black plays c5 to challenge d4; after White captures, Nc6 enters with immediate counterattacking threats.

name: Owen Defense: Matovinsky Gambit
description: Black sacrifices the f-pawn and bishop for rapid central counterplay; Black stabilizes with g6.

name: Owen Defense: Naselwaus Gambit
description: White develops the bishop to g5, pinning Black's fianchettoed b7 bishop after b6.

name: Owen Defense: Smith Gambit
description: Black fianchettoes and White develops Nf3, pursuing a classical setup against Black's structure.

name: Owen Defense: Unicorn Variation
description: Black fianchettoes both kingside and queenside, controlling key diagonals with paired bishops.

name: Owen Defense: Wind Gambit
description: White plays f3 after Black fianchettoes; Black strikes back with e5, creating central tension.

name: Pirc Defense: Roscher Gambit
description: White develops Nf3 against Black's d6 and Nf6 setup, maintaining a classical centre.

name: Rat Defense: Antal Defense
description: Black develops the knight to d7 after d6, preparing a flexible fianchetto or e5 advance.

name: Rat Defense: Fuller Gambit
description: White sacrifices with f4 and e4; Black captures d5 and develops Nf6 for active piece play.

name: Rat Defense: Harmonist
description: White plays f4 immediately to control e5 and claim kingside space against Black's modest d6.

name: Rat Defense: Petruccioli Attack
description: White plays h4 to launch rapid kingside expansion and potentially prepare a kingside assault.

name: Rat Defense: Spike Attack
description: White plays g4 to expand immediately on the kingside, sacrificing pawn structure for attacking chances.

name: St. George Defense: Polish Variation
description: Black plays a6 and b5 for queenside space, fianchettoes, and supports with e6 for solidity.

name: St. George Defense: San Jorge Variation
description: Black builds a double fianchetto setup on both wings with careful development and piece coordination.

name: St. George Defense: Zilbermints Gambit
description: Black plays a6 then immediately strikes with e5, contesting White's centre despite flank play.

name: Van Geet Opening: Berlin Gambit
description: After captures and Nc3, White plays d5 to gain space and displace Black's centralized knight.

name: Ware Defense: Snagglepuss Defense
description: Black plays a5 immediately and develops Nc6, pursuing offbeat queenside play and piece coordination.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Anderssen Counterattack
description: Black plays e5 to contest d4 aggressively, obtaining active piece play despite the exposed queen.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Anderssen Counterattack, Collijn Variation
description: Black develops Bg4 to pin the Nf3 and maintain pressure on White's centre and development.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Anderssen Counterattack, Goteborg System
description: White develops with Nf3, leading to a solid setup where both sides have clear piece placement and plans.
